reason: The frozen E1 fit uses a ridge penalty normalised per unit of forecast (objective in e1_layer.py). On FIT data only, this shrinks rare one-day effects strongly: Christmas day-0 was estimated at a 0.86 daily multiplier, while FIT data show a store closure (0 units on 2012-12-25 across 2,359 series; 4 units on 2013-12-25 across 2,771). This diagnosis used FIT data only; SEL results of the original candidates were seen (all slightly worse than base) before this amendment, so SEL is a SECOND LOOK for these new candidates and their SEL results are less clean.

new_candidates.E1c: calendar closure rule, no learned parameters: closure days known from the calendar (US: 25 December, established from FIT data); adjusted = F * (h - closed days in the window) / h
new_candidates.E1w: same E1 form, penalty per coefficient scaled by that coefficient's share of exposure-weighted forecast units (rare events are not over-shrunk); levels pooled and pooled+category; alpha in [0.1, 1, 10]; Christmas|d0 excluded from learned features
new_candidates.E1cw: E1c for closure days, then E1w on the remaining events

selection: unchanged rule: highest mean relative event-window WAPE improvement over both horizons on SEL; all original candidates stay in the comparison; gates of proposal section 8.5 reported descriptively
